name: ラーメンムギュ Vol.2 烏丸蛸薬師店 (Ramen Mugyu Vol.2 Karasuma Takoyakushi)

claims.text: The signature bowls use a soy-sauce (shoyu) based tare, and conventional shoyu is brewed with wheat — this is the seasoning backbone of the broth.
The shoyu (soy sauce) tare that flavors the broth is standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.

name: ラーメン大蔵 一乗寺店 (Ramen Okura Ichijoji-ten)

claims.text: Shoyu and shio tare at a standard Japanese ramen shop are made with conventional wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free soy sauce is indicated.
Broths are animal-based (pork/chicken and a ten-fish seafood blend) and the shared kitchen also fries karaage and cooks gyoza, so no plant-based bowl can be assumed clean.

name: らーめん千の風 四条河原町店 (Ramen Sen no Kaze Shijo-Kawaramachi)

claims.text: The 京の醤油 (Kyoto soy sauce) ramen is built on a soy-sauce tare, which in standard Japanese ramen contains wheat.

name: ラーメン専門店 大輝 (Ramen Senmonten Daiki)

claims.text: The ramen uses wheat noodles cooked in shared water and a wheat-based light soy-sauce tare; there is no gluten-free preparation or separate handling.
The bowl is seasoned with a light soy-sauce (薄口醤油) tare, which is wheat-based as standard Japanese soy sauce.
The broth is a pork bone stock and the bowl is topped with pork chashu, so all menu items are animal-based; no vegan options exist.

name: ラーメン荘 地球規模で考えろ 伏見本店 (Ramen So Chikyu Kibo de Kangaero (Fushimi Ho)

claims.text: Bowls center on house-made wheat noodles boiled in a shared pot; there is no gluten-free preparation, so cross-contamination is unavoidable.
The broth is seasoned with a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, which in a Jiro-style shop is virtually always wheat-containing soy sauce.
All bowls share a pork-bone broth and pork back-fat; vegetable, garlic and fat toppings are added on top of the animal broth, so no bowl is free of animal products.

name: ラーメン荘 夢を語れ (Ramen-sou Yume wo Katare)

claims.text: The bowl is built on ultra-thick hand-kneaded wheat noodles, a wheat-based shoyu tare, and pork-bone broth; gluten is unavoidable and there is no GF preparation.
The broth is a soy-sauce (shoyu) seasoned pork-bone base; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Every bowl contains pork chashu, pork-bone broth, and back fat (背脂); no vegan or vegetarian preparation exists.

name: ラーメンとまぜそばのお店 Lee (Ramen to Mazesoba no Omise Lee)

claims.text: Wheat ramen and mazesoba noodles from Kyoto maker Menya Teigaku (棣鄂) are the base of every bowl, cooked in a shared single-counter kitchen, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Bowls use wheat-based shoyu/curry sauces (e.g. gyokai-shoyu mazesoba and shoyu-seasoned ramen), which contain wheat.
Broths are chicken/pork-bone based and mazesoba/keema use ground meat, house-made bacon, egg yolk, cheese and pork back fat; no plant-based preparation exists.
